source: NCERT Class XII, An Introduction to Indian Art (Part 2), Ch. 2 (The Rajasthani Schools of Painting).

sections.heading: 1. Rajasthani (Rajput) Painting — Overview
points: **Rajasthani painting** flourished in the courts of **Rajputana (Rajasthan)** from the 16th–19th centuries.
Themes: **religious (Krishna-Radha, Ragamala, Barahmasa), epics, court life, hunting, portraits**.
Style: **bold colours, flat perspective, decorative, emotional (bhava)** — distinct from Mughal realism.

sections.heading: 2. Major Sub-Schools
points: **Mewar (Udaipur)** — one of the earliest; e.g. the **Ragamala** series by **Nisardi/Sahibdin**.
**Bundi and Kota** — famous for **hunting scenes** and lush landscapes; vivid nature.
**Kishangarh** — famous for the idealised female figure **'Bani Thani'** (by **Nihal Chand**), with elongated eyes/features (the 'Indian Mona Lisa').
**Marwar (Jodhpur), Bikaner, Jaipur (Amber)** — distinctive court styles.

sections.heading: 3. Themes and Ragamala
points: **Ragamala** paintings — visual depictions of musical **ragas** (melodies personified).
**Barahmasa** — the twelve months; **Nayaka-Nayika** (hero-heroine) themes; **Krishna-lila** (Gita Govinda, Bhagavata Purana).
Painting was closely tied to **Vaishnava bhakti** (devotion to Krishna).

sections.heading: 4. Style and Legacy
points: Marked by **flat, bright colour planes, stylised figures, and lyrical/emotional content**.
Rajasthani painting is more **indigenous and devotional** than the Mughal school (though it absorbed some Mughal influence).
It preserved regional identity and Hindu themes.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Rajasthani schools: Mewar, Bundi-Kota, Kishangarh, Marwar, Bikaner, Jaipur.
Kishangarh = 'Bani Thani' (by Nihal Chand), 'Indian Mona Lisa'.
Bundi-Kota = hunting scenes and landscapes.
Themes: Ragamala, Barahmasa, Krishna-Radha (Vaishnava bhakti).
Style: bold flat colours, decorative, emotional (vs Mughal realism).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **'Bani Thani' = Kishangarh school** (Nihal Chand).
**Bundi and Kota** are famous for **hunting scenes**.
**Ragamala** paintings depict **musical ragas**.
Rajasthani painting uses **bold flat colours** (unlike Mughal realism/perspective).
